text: The 40 members of a club include Ranuf and Saed. All 40 members will travel to a concert.
35 members will travel in a coach and the other 5 will travel in a car. Ranuf will be in the coach and
Saed will be in the car.
In how many ways can the members who will travel in the coach be chosen? [3]

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Find the probability that it takes at least 3 throws but no more than 5 throws to obtain a 1 or a 6.

On another occasion, this die is thrown 3 times. The random variable X is the number of times that
a 1 or a 6 is obtained.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Draw up the probability distribution table for X.

text: An ordinary fair die is thrown repeatedly until a 1 or a 6 is obtained.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Find the standard deviation of the weights of these apples.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Find the probability that the weight of a randomly chosen apple of this variety differs from the
mean weight by less than 4 grams.

text: The weights of apples of a certain variety are normally distributed with mean 82 grams. 22% of these
apples have a weight greater than 87 grams.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Find the number of different arrangements of the 11 candles if there is a red candle at each end.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Find the number of different arrangements of the 11 candles if all the blue candles are together
and the red candles are not together.

text: Richard has 3 blue candles, 2 red candles and 6 green candles. The candles are identical apart from
their colours. He arranges the 11 candles in a line.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Find the probability that the number of adults in this sample who own a car is less than 6. 
A random sample of 120 adults from Greenton is now chosen.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Use an approximation to find the probability that more than 75 of them own a car.

text: In Greenton, 70% of the adults own a car. A random sample of 8 adults from Greenton is chosen.

Find the probability that the ball chosen from box A is blue given that the ball chosen from box B

text: Box A contains 7 red balls and 1 blue ball. Box B contains 9 red balls and 5 blue balls. A ball is
chosen at random from box A and placed in box B. A ball is then chosen at random from box B. The
tree diagram below shows the possibilities for the colours of the balls chosen.

parts.text: Draw a cumulative frequency graph to illustrate the data.

parts.text:
40% of these fish have a length of d cm or more. Use your graph to estimate the value of d. 
The mean length of these 150 fish is 15.295 cm.

Calculate an estimate for the variance of the lengths of the fish.
